summary: 29-year-old at 22 weeks’ gestation with 36 h of RUQ pain, fever 38.2 °C, positive Murphy’s; WBC 14.8 and ALP 210 (both partly physiological in pregnancy); ultrasound shows gallstones with a 5 mm wall and pericholecystic fluid; live fetus.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Right upper abdominal pain and fever in pregnancy
inputs.hpi: G2P1 at 22 weeks. 36 hours of constant right upper quadrant pain after a fried meal, with fever and vomiting. Similar short episodes earlier in the pregnancy. Fetal movements normal; no vaginal bleeding, no contractions. No jaundice.

exam.general: Unwell. Temperature 38.2°C, pulse 104/min, BP 116/70. Gravid uterus, fundus at the umbilicus.
exam.abdomen: Right upper quadrant tenderness with positive Murphy's sign. Uterus soft and non-tender.

imaging.name: USS abdomen
imaging.result: Gallstones with a stone in the gallbladder neck; wall 5 mm with pericholecystic fluid; sonographic Murphy's positive. CBD 5 mm. Single live intrauterine fetus, FHR 148/min.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Acute calculous cholecystitis
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Acute calculous cholecystitis, Tokyo (TG18) Grade I, at 22 weeks’ gestation.

emergencyLevel.note: Same-day surgical and obstetric assessment. iOS (predicted, not observed): routine — the CC has no urgent keyword and "right upper" selects the biliary pathway, which only escalates for jaundice/cholangitis.

redFlags.note: Pregnancy must be surfaced before imaging, drugs or theatre.

values.note: WBC 14.8 is below the Grade II threshold (and partly physiological in pregnancy).

mustExclude.note: US (and MRI/MRCP if needed) preferred; CT is not contraindicated but should not be the unqualified default.

mustInclude.note: SAGES 2017: laparoscopic cholecystectomy is safe in any trimester and reduces recurrence and fetal loss compared with conservative management.

mustExclude.note: NSAIDs should be avoided from 20 weeks’ gestation.
The patient is pregnant; templates must not assert a negative pregnancy test.
Not an appendix presentation: an appendicectomy operative plan (consent, theatre booking, post-operative orders) is a wrong-procedure suggestion.

guideline.name: Tokyo Guidelines 2018 — diagnostic criteria and severity grading of acute cholecystitis
guideline.section: Diagnostic criteria (A local + B systemic + C imaging); Grade II: WBC >18,000/mm³, palpable tender RUQ mass, duration >72 h, marked local inflammation (gangrenous, emphysematous, abscess, biliary peritonitis); Grade III: organ dysfunction
guideline.citation: Yokoe M, Hata J, Takada T, et al. J Hepatobiliary Pancreat Sci. 2018;25:41–54.

guideline.name: Tokyo Guidelines 2018 — antimicrobial therapy for acute cholangitis and cholecystitis
guideline.section: Blood cultures in Grade II/III; antimicrobial choice by severity; duration after source control
guideline.citation: Gomi H, Solomkin JS, Schlossberg D, et al. J Hepatobiliary Pancreat Sci. 2018;25:3–16.

guideline.name: SAGES guidelines for the use of laparoscopy during pregnancy
guideline.section: Laparoscopic cholecystectomy is safe in any trimester and is the treatment of choice for symptomatic gallbladder disease/gallstone pancreatitis; obstetric consultation; fetal heart monitoring; VTE prophylaxis
guideline.citation: Pearl JP, Price RR, Tonkin AE, Richardson WS, Stefanidis D. Surg Endosc. 2017;31:3767–3782.

guideline.name: ACOG Committee Opinion No. 723 — Guidelines for diagnostic imaging during pregnancy and lactation
guideline.section: US and MRI preferred; CT not contraindicated when needed; gadolinium only if it clearly improves diagnosis
guideline.citation: ACOG Committee Opinion No. 723. Obstet Gynecol. 2017;130:e210–e216.

guideline.name: ACOG Committee Opinion No. 775 — Nonobstetric surgery during pregnancy
guideline.section: Obstetric consultation before non-obstetric surgery; fetal heart rate assessment before and after the procedure
guideline.citation: ACOG Committee Opinion No. 775. Obstet Gynecol. 2019;133:e285–e286.

guideline.name: US FDA Drug Safety Communication — NSAIDs in pregnancy at 20 weeks or later
guideline.section: Avoid NSAIDs from about 20 weeks’ gestation (fetal renal dysfunction, oligohydramnios)
guideline.citation: US Food and Drug Administration. Drug Safety Communication, 15 October 2020.

rationale: Permutation: pregnancy in the second trimester. Tests the pregnancy flag, that physiological leucocytosis/ALP do not over-grade, that cholecystectomy is still offered (SAGES), and that NSAIDs, unqualified CT and teratogenic antibiotics are avoided.
